page.tagline: Convert 180°C to Fahrenheit, find fan oven and air fryer equivalents, baking times, and USDA safe internal temperatures.
page.customIntro: 180 degrees Celsius equals 356 degrees Fahrenheit, calculated as (180 × 9/5) + 32 = 356°F. This is the most common conventional oven temperature for baking cakes, cookies, and roasting vegetables. For fan ovens or air fryers, reduce to 160°C (320°F). In Gas Mark terms, 180°C corresponds to Gas Mark 4.

about.title: About 180°C / 356°F: Why It Is the Default Baking Temperature
about.paragraph1: 180°C (356°F) is the standard baking temperature because it triggers the Maillard reaction (starting around 140°C / 285°F and peaking near 165°C / 330°F) while staying below the burning point of most sugars (approximately 180°C for sucrose). This means food browns and develops flavor without scorching. At 180°C, most cake batters set their protein structure within 25–35 minutes, long enough for the center to cook through but fast enough to avoid over-browning.
about.paragraph2: Home ovens are often inaccurate: real-world testing shows many run 25–50°F (14–28°C) hotter or cooler than the set temperature. An oven set to 180°C might actually be 155°C or 205°C. A $10–20 oven thermometer is the single most effective tool for consistent baking results.

bakingTimes.title: Baking Times at 180°C (356°F)
bakingTimes.intro: These are typical baking times at 180°C in a conventional oven. Always check doneness with a toothpick or thermometer rather than relying on time alone.

rows.doneness: Skewer comes out clean, top springs back
Slight wobble in center, edges pulling away
Golden top, skewer comes out clean

bakingTimes.note: Times assume a conventional oven. For fan ovens or air fryers, reduce time by 20–25% and check doneness early.

foodSafety.title: USDA Safe Internal Temperatures
foodSafety.intro: Oven temperature is not the same as food internal temperature. The USDA recommends these minimum internal temperatures to ensure food is safe to eat, measured with a food thermometer inserted into the thickest part.
foodSafety.source: Source: USDA FoodSafety.gov (last reviewed November 2024). Always use a food thermometer to verify doneness.

whatNotToBake.title: What NOT to Bake at 180°C
whatNotToBake.intro: 180°C is versatile, but some foods require a different temperature for proper results. Using the wrong temperature leads to cracked surfaces, burnt edges, or undercooked centers.

items.reason: Use 120–160°C — 180°C browns and cracks the delicate structure.
Use 160°C — 180°C causes cracking without a water bath.
Use 190–200°C — needs high heat for steam and layer separation.
Use 200–220°C — needs high heat for oven spring and crust.
Use 220°C+ — needs intense heat for blistered crust.
Use 150–160°C in a water bath — 180°C scrambles the eggs.

troubleshooting.title: Baking Troubleshooting at 180°C
troubleshooting.intro: If your bakes at 180°C are not turning out right, the problem is often oven accuracy, rack position, or pan choice. Here are the most common issues and how to fix them.

rows.cause: Oven runs hot, or food too close to heat source
rows.fix: Lower to 170°C, move rack to center, use an oven thermometer to verify.

rows.cause: Underbaked, or too much leavening agent
rows.fix: Extend baking time by 5–10 min, reduce baking powder by 1/4 tsp.

rows.cause: Oven runs cool, or oven door opened too early
rows.fix: Raise to 190°C, avoid opening the door before 20 minutes.

rows.cause: Dark pan absorbs more heat, or rack too low
rows.fix: Move rack up one position, double-pan, or use a lighter-colored pan.

rows.cause: Oven too hot, or batter overfilled
rows.fix: Reduce to 170°C, fill pans no more than 2/3 full.

faq.question: What is 180 degrees Celsius in Fahrenheit?
faq.answer: 180 degrees Celsius equals 356 degrees Fahrenheit. The conversion formula is °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32, so (180 × 1.8) + 32 = 356°F.

faq.question: Is 180°C the same as 350°F?
faq.answer: Not exactly. 180°C equals 356°F, not 350°F. However, 350°F converts to 176.7°C, so many recipes round to 180°C for convenience. The 6°F difference is small enough that most bakes turn out fine either way.

faq.question: What is 180°C in a fan oven or air fryer?
faq.answer: For fan ovens and air fryers, reduce 180°C by 20°C to 160°C (320°F). Fan circulation cooks food approximately 20% faster, so also check doneness 5–10 minutes earlier than the recipe states.

faq.question: What Gas Mark is 180°C?
faq.answer: 180°C corresponds to Gas Mark 4. This is the standard setting for cakes, cookies, and everyday baking on gas ovens. Gas Mark 4 equals approximately 180°C (356°F).

faq.question: How long to bake a cake at 180°C?
faq.answer: Most sponge cakes bake in 25–30 minutes at 180°C in a conventional oven. A 900g banana bread loaf takes 50–60 minutes. Always test doneness with a skewer — it should come out clean when inserted into the center.

faq.question: Can I bake bread at 180°C?
faq.answer: 180°C is too low for most bread. Crusty loaves need 200–220°C for proper oven spring and crust formation. Soft rolls can work at 180°C, but expect a lighter crust. For sourdough or artisan bread, use at least 220°C.

faq.question: Why do my cakes crack on top at 180°C?
faq.answer: Cakes crack when the oven runs hotter than the set temperature, causing the top to set before the center finishes rising. Use an oven thermometer to verify accuracy. If the oven is correct, reduce to 170°C and avoid filling pans more than two-thirds full.

faq.question: How do I adjust 180°C for high altitude baking?
faq.answer: Above 3,000 feet (915 m), increase oven temperature by 25°F (14°C) and reduce baking time by 10–15%. You may also need to decrease sugar and increase liquid. At 5,000+ feet, further adjustments are needed — consult USDA high-altitude baking guides.
